note: CKEditor(5) Emoji is a pure client-side CKEditor 5 plugin (ckeditor_emoji_Emoji / emojiPlugin.Emoji) that contributes an 'Emoji' toolbar button. It has no PHP settings form, no configure route (configure=null), no permissions, no config schema, no Drush and no Drupal plugin types. Its only persistent footprint is the 'Emoji' string added to a text format's CKEditor 5 toolbar, stored in editor.editor.<format> -> settings.toolbar.items. It depends on core ckeditor5 and works only with CKEditor 5. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real editor config: introspection reads back which CKEditor 5 format has the Emoji button; execution adds the Emoji button to a format's toolbar, verified against the live editor.editor entity.

evals.prompt: I installed the Drupal contrib module ckeditor_emoji. There is no settings page for it. How do I actually make the emoji button appear for content authors, and where is that choice saved?
evals.expected_output: There is no configure route (configure=null). You add the Emoji button to a text format's CKEditor 5 toolbar at Configuration > Content authoring > Text formats and editors (/admin/config/content/formats): drag the Emoji button into the Active toolbar and save. It is stored in editor.editor.<format> -> settings.toolbar.items as the string 'Emoji'.

evals.prompt: Which CKEditor version does the Drupal ckeditor_emoji module work with, and what core module does it require?
evals.expected_output: It is a CKEditor 5 plugin and depends on Drupal core's ckeditor5 module (core_version_requirement ^10.3 || ^11). It is the CKEditor 5 successor to the older CKEditor 4 'Emoji' module and does not work with CKEditor 4.

evals.prompt: Does enabling the emoji button in ckeditor_emoji require me to change a text format's allowed HTML tags or add a filter? How is an emoji inserted into the content?
evals.expected_output: No allowed-tags or filter change is needed. The CKEditor5 plugin declares elements: false, so picking an emoji inserts a plain Unicode character via CKEditor's input command - no new HTML tags or data-model markup are added.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one CKEditor 5 text format has the ckeditor_emoji 'Emoji' button enabled in its toolbar. Inspect the live editor configuration and give the machine name (format id) of that text format.
evals.expected_output: The format is ckemoji_known: editor.editor.ckemoji_known settings.toolbar.items contains 'Emoji'.

evals.prompt: This site has two CKEditor 5 text formats, ckemoji_on and ckemoji_off. Exactly one of them has the ckeditor_emoji Emoji button in its toolbar. Inspect the live editor configuration and state which format has emoji enabled.
evals.expected_output: ckemoji_on has the Emoji button: editor.editor.ckemoji_on settings.toolbar.items includes 'Emoji', whereas ckemoji_off's toolbar does not.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a CKEditor 5 text format with id 'ckemoji_task' that does not yet have the emoji picker. Using the ckeditor_emoji module, add the Emoji button to that format's CKEditor 5 toolbar and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add the string 'Emoji' to editor.editor.ckemoji_task settings.toolbar.items (drag the Emoji button into the Active toolbar in the text-format UI, or append 'Emoji' to the toolbar items and save the editor entity).

evals.prompt: People writing with my 'ckemoji_task' text style can't add smiley faces or emojis. Please turn on the emoji picker so the little emoji button shows up in their editor toolbar, and make it live on the site.
evals.expected_output: Add the Emoji button (string 'Emoji') to the ckemoji_task format's CKEditor 5 toolbar (editor.editor.ckemoji_task settings.toolbar.items) via the Text formats and editors UI or by saving the editor entity.
